issues.title: Wrong sign in the nonlocal Landau gradient-flow equation
issues.failure_explanation: Let the flux be the quantity inside the old nonlocal divergence. Equation 0910 gives the weak evolution as minus one half of the pairing of the nonlocal gradient with that flux. By new_div, this pairing is minus the pairing of the test function with the nonlocal divergence. The two minus signs therefore give ∂_t f equal to positive one half of the divergence. The old equation instead asserts the negative of this evolution.
issues.overall_effect: The labeled strong-form equation reverses the Landau evolution relative to the immediately preceding weak formulation and misstates the gradient-flow orientation. No canonically identified formal result relies specifically on the erroneous sign.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change (landau_weak3) to place a minus sign before the nonlocal divergence term, equivalently writing ∂_t f as positive one half of that divergence. No dependent formal result requires modification.
issues.why_classification: The old weak identity (0910), the adjoint definition (new_div), and the opening Landau equation uniquely force the corrected sign. This is a transcriptional sign error whose one-symbol correction requires no new argument and causes no loss in the recorded affected chain.

issues.title: Malformed product domain in the entropy-dissipation condition
issues.failure_explanation: The integrand depends independently on \(v\) and \(v_*\), and the measure is \(dv\,dv_*\), so its integration domain is the product \(\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d=\mathbb R^{2d}\). The old \(\iint_{\mathbb R^d}\) is dimensionally incompatible with those two variables. The equivalent instantaneous dissipation in the latest version is correctly defined on \(\mathbb R^{2d}\) and required to lie in \(L^1([0,T])\).
issues.overall_effect: The weak-solution dissipation condition is malformed, and the generated Landau gradient-flow theorem inherits it through assumption (iii). The intended admissible class remains evident from the neighboring two-particle formulas.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the domain R^d under the double integral in (entropy_diss) by R^{2d}=R^d×R^d. The dependent theorem's assumption (iii) then invokes the corrected condition without any further change.
issues.why_classification: The two independent variables v and v_* and the measure dv dv_* uniquely force the product domain. Correcting the malformed integral subscript is purely notational and preserves the admissible class and every guarantee of the dependent theorem.

issues.title: Absolute value is misplaced in the log-Jacobian proposition
issues.failure_explanation: For a nonzero Jacobian determinant, the signed log-Jacobian evolution is the derivative of \(\log|\det\nabla T_t|\). The old quantity \(|\log\det\nabla T_t|\) instead introduces a factor equal to the sign of the logarithm and can be nondifferentiable when the determinant equals one. Thus its displayed derivative does not equal the signed divergence expression asserted on the right. The old downstream formulation already uses the supported quantity \(\log|\det|\).
issues.overall_effect: The unlabelled proposition states the wrong log-Jacobian evolution. Later particle and JKO formulas already use the intended placement of the absolute value, so no later canonical formal result is defeated by this transcription error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace d/dt |log det ∇T_t| by d/dt log |det ∇T_t| in the proposition, leaving the right-hand side unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The standard log-Jacobian identity and the old downstream Lagrangian formulation already use log |det|, uniquely identifying the misplaced absolute-value bars. The proposition is repaired by transcription alone, with no proof reconstruction or downstream loss.

issues.title: Undeclared initial-score input in the JKO particle algorithm

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $N$ initial particles $\{\bv_i^0\}_{i=1}^N \stackrel{i.i.d.}\sim f^0$; JKO time step $\tau$ and total number of JKO steps $N_T$.

issues.failure_explanation: The input contract lists initial particles sampled from \(f^0\), the time step, and the number of steps. Minimizing L2_loss additionally requires every value \(\nabla\log f^0(v_i^0)\). A finite particle sample does not provide those derivatives, so the initialization instruction is not executable from the declared inputs unless an unstated score oracle is supplied.
issues.overall_effect: The score-based preinitialization step is undefined under the algorithm's stated interface. The JKO loss, particle update, and formal structural properties do not otherwise depend on this initialization choice.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the mandatory score-fitting preinitialization by a standard declared initialization of the initial neural network that uses only the available inputs. The score-based warm start may instead be described as optional when score evaluations are separately supplied; retain all JKO training and particle-update steps.
issues.why_classification: The unavailable score values create a genuine executable-interface defect and there is a choice between adding an oracle and removing the warm start, so this is not a typo. However, the preinitialization is only a training convenience: a local generic initialization preserves the JKO objective, particle updates, input class, and recorded structural guarantees without any new lemma or substantive loss.
